name: yappal-ideas-scoreboard
rule: Pre-registered (ios/IDEAS-SUPER.md 1). Every number on the scoreboard branch is computed by .github/scoreboard/*.js from the values in this file. Each published day carries one hash of this file and of the scoring code (comparators.js, history.js, match.js, metrics.js, ours.js, report.js, stats.js); a change to any value or any of those files changes the hash and restarts the 14-day clock.

scoredDay.why: The run at 06:20Z scores the UTC day two days before it: an entry that surfaced at 23:59 that day has had its 24 hours to be listed, and the 18:00 list of that day its 24 hours to be checked.

handle.needs: a digit or a capital inside the word

person.rule: only for person trends: the comparator's whole title is the name of a person the row names; the row's own title is that name and at most 2 more title-core words; the name has two words or more or is a handle (one word of 6+ characters with a digit or a capital inside it)

bareName.rule: a join whose comparator entry is, by its title core, only the name of a person the row names (or the row's subject) holds only when corroborated: the entry's related searches share a title-core word, tag or other person with the row beyond the entry's own words, or the entry surfaced between 24 h before and 48 h after our first listing of the row. Compared as title cores, so stopwords and framing words around a name ('X now', 'where is X from', 'X news') leave it a bare name

longLead.rule: any join whose entry surfaced more than hoursAfterListing (48 h) after our first listing of the row, on a comparator that gives related searches, holds only when those related searches corroborate it as above (a time near our listing cannot corroborate a lead that long). Know Your Meme, the Viral 50 and X give none and are not held to it

ours.listed: our first listing of a trend: the first sample of the collector's own read (neither backfilled nor reseeded) that ranks it 1 to listDepth in the US list; a compacted hour or day counts from its start, never before the collector's first_listed_at
ours.firstPage: when a trend first reached page one: the first such sample that ranks it 1 to page; a compacted bucket counts from its start, never before first_page_at
ours.excluded: from lead: trends met in the state's first 3 hours (its first cycle or a reseed) and trends read back from the feed (reseeded); from lead and coverage: entries that surfaced before the cold start ended or less than 24 h before the state's newest sample

sighting.gt: the first sample of the trend with sv_us > 0 (the collector's own Google Trends read showing it)
sighting.kym: seenFirst of the entry's address in the state's store rows
sighting.viral50: first_seen of the sound in platform_items (source tts, viral chart), or the scoreboard's own first read

kym.name: Know Your Meme, confirmed and submitted entries
kym.depth: 16 a feed as served, both feeds, one entry per address

viral50.name: Trending TikTok Songs, US Viral 50

scope.chart: the chart dated the scored day, else the next day's, else the day before's

viral50.own: 00:00Z of the first chart day the sound was seen on (not known for sounds on the scoreboard's first read: left out of lead)

x.name: X trends, US, via getdaytrends
x.refused: a refused or unreadable reply leaves X unmeasured that day; nothing else is tried

lead.definition: per shared trend (one of our trends matched to an entry that surfaced in the day): surface minus our first listing, hours; surface = the earlier of the entry's own time and our own first read showing it
lead.tie: listed at or after our own read of that comparator showed it: lead 0

window.rule: a matched pair counts when our first listing falls within 7 days either side of its surface, and every such pair is in n: first when listed before the surface, tie when listed at or after our own read of that comparator showed it, else late with its real hours

lead.onePerTrend: a trend matched to several entries counts once, at the earliest surface

listedLate.rule: a sub-count of the late pairs: listed more than 24 h after the surface. They stay in n

coverage.definition: share of the comparator's scope entries of the day which we listed between 7 days before and 24 h after the entry's anchor
coverage.anchor: Google Trends and Know Your Meme: the entry's own time (its start, its pubDate); the Viral 50: the scored day's start (that day's chart); X: the snapshot's time

split.first: listed before the surface: the earlier of the entry's own time and our own read of that comparator showing it (the anchor when neither is known), the rule lead uses

coverage.insufficient: under minN scope entries, a day (or the rolling window) reads insufficient: no share

breadth.definition: new stories over new Google Trends scope entries, flow over flow: distinct stories that first reached page one that day (shared, or only here and confirmed), over the Google Trends scope entries that started that day
breadth.stories: the page-one rows of the day's archived lists (09:00 and 18:00 US time), joined into one story when the matcher joins their titles; a story's first page one is the earliest of its rows' (ours.firstPage), and it counts on that day only
breadth.shared: matched to any comparator entry that surfaced within 7 days either side of the story's first page one

onlyHere.source: the collector's own outlets column (its count of independent outlets) in the 48 h before to 24 h after the story's first page one: the collector's count, not an item the scoreboard checks itself, so a change to the collector's clustering or outlet counting moves it without a spec change

breadth.pooled: pooled over lead.poolDays days under one spec hash before it counts toward the target and the claim; under minN Google Trends starts (a day, the pool or the rolling window), insufficient: no ratio
breadth.coldStart: both halves count from the end of the state's cold start (ours.coldStartHours after its first cycle or a reseed): a story on page one in those hours is not known to be new, and Google Trends starts in those hours are not counted either

precision.definition: page one of each archived list of the day (09:00 and 18:00 US time), checked 24 hours later
precision.fading: status fading on a measured series in the archived row
precision.duplicate: a page-one row the matcher joins to a row ranked above it

speed.definition: from the ledger lines whose slot falls in the day: publish lag (published minus slot) median and p90, and the mean age of the feed at a random moment (minutes since the slot of the newest published feed, integrated over the day)

claim.rule: 3x is claimed only when lead (pooled 7 days) and breadth (pooled 7 days) meet target with the precision gate holding, 14 consecutive published days under one spec hash

cache.holds: the comparators' entries and read statuses of the last days, and each scored day's lead values (hours and outcome: no name, id or instant) and breadth counts. Never a matched pair or anything of ours per trend: a fork's pull request can restore this repository's caches
